name: Kenya Sentinel
blurb: A few weeks ago, I built a real-time YouTube toxicity tracker using AWS Kinesis and AWS Comprehend. It worked. It was fast. But it felt like a "black box." I wanted to see under the hood, so I tore it down and rebuilt it from scratch using Apache Kafka and a custom Scikit-Learn model.
notes: The Experience: It’s incredibly polished. You plug things in, pay your bill, and it works.
The Catch: I was limited by what AWS thought "Negative" meant. I had no control over the "why."
The Experience: I had to manage the broker, handle the message offsets, and train the model myself.
The biggest shift wasn't just the tools—it was the logic.
In my AWS version, I got back a label: "Negative." In my custom Kafka version, I get back a Raw Risk Score (e.g., 87.4%).

By leveraging my own Logistic Regression model, I stopped letting a pre-built API decide what was "Toxic." I built a Risk Threshold slider in React that allows the end-user to decide the sensitivity. If you want to see only the absolute worst 95% risk
